findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow has independent status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool fields, allowing illegal state combinations such as status="draft" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_sent=false and is_validated=false. The domain invariant that only one lifecycle phase is active at a time is not enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller (including internal) can set is_sent=true while leaving status="draft", or set status="sent" without is_sent=true, producing logically inconsistent records that downstream code cannot reason about safely.
findings.fix: Replace status: String and the two bool flags with a single enum BudgetState (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent) with a sent_at field only present on Sent. Remove all pub fields; expose via an immutable struct with methods.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing any module to mutate id, status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms directly. This defeats encapsulation and makes it impossible to enforce invariants at assignment time.
findings.failure_mode: A caller in the imperative shell can mutate is_validated=false while setting is_sent=true, bypassing the mark_sent logic entirely and corrupting state without any constructor check.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a private constructor that enforces invariants, and expose only read-only accessors or state-transition methods on immutable self references.

findings.problem: status is a raw String rather than a domain enum. This allows arbitrary string values (e.g., status="sent", status="SENT", status="PENDING") that are semantically indistinguishable or contradictory to the bool flags.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, case mismatches, or unknown values in status create silent logic bugs. Pattern matching on status requires string comparison rather than exhaustive enum matching, risking unhandled cases.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum: pub enum BudgetStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Fold is_validated and is_sent into the enum variants so only one lifecycle phase exists at a time.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of BudgetWorkflow and mutates it in-place (item.status = "sent".to_string(); item.is_sent = true), then returns it. This is an imperative mutation pattern in what should be a pure calculation. The function has side effects (allocating a new String) and modifies fields rather than returning a new valid state.
findings.failure_mode: The function allocates a new String on every call even when status was already "sent", and the caller loses the original value with no way to observe what changed. In a functional core, transitions should be pure functions from old state to new state with allocation only at the shell boundary.
findings.fix: Change signature to fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError> with a typestate-gated transition. Return a new BudgetWorkflow with the single enum state, no in-place mutation, and error if already in terminal state.

findings.problem: id is a raw String rather than a domain newtype (e.g., BudgetId). This allows passing any string where a budget ID is expected, mixing up IDs with other string fields.
findings.failure_mode: A caller could pass a status string where a budget ID is expected, or compare budget IDs against other strings, with the compiler unable to catch the mismatch.
findings.fix: Introduce pub struct BudgetId(String) with Display/Debug impls. Use BudgetId as the field type.

findings.problem: There is no constructor for BudgetWorkflow. All fields are pub, so callers can construct the struct with arbitrary invalid combinations. No validation runs at construction time.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can create BudgetWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } which represents no valid lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Remove pub from all fields. Add impl BudgetWorkflow { pub fn new(id: BudgetId) -> Self { ... } } or use a builder that enforces invariants. If construction is always internal, make fields private with a doc-private new().

findings.problem: No validation of sent_at_epoch_ms (e.g., non-zero, monotonic) when entering the Sent state. The Option<u64> allows None or 0 as a valid sent timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: A sent budget with sent_at_epoch_ms=None or 0 could pass downstream checks that assume a real timestamp, causing incorrect ordering, sorting, or TTL calculations.
findings.fix: Use NonZero<u64> or a positive-checked u64 for sent_at_epoch_ms. When the state transitions to Sent, require a non-zero timestamp.

residual_risk: High. The domain model permits all illegal state combinations through pub primitive fields with no typestate enforcement. mark_sent performs in-place mutation instead of pure state transition. Without enum-based lifecycle representation, any downstream code making assumptions about valid state is fundamentally unsound. Static review only; no commands executed.
